headline: India's central bank chief listed AI-driven valuations and AI-powered cyber attacks among five threats to global financial stability.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a central-bank governor on the record, echoing warnings from the Bank of England the same week.
importance_line: A slowdown in AI investment or earnings could trigger a sharp fall in asset prices that would hit savers and leveraged funds first, the RBI governor warns, while stressing that none of the five risks is alarming on its own yet.
summary: Hindustan Times reports that Reserve Bank of India governor Sanjay Malhotra told the Kautilya Economic Conclave in New Delhi on Saturday that high global debt, stretched asset valuations driven by the AI investment cycle, rising leverage, private credit and cyber risk heightened by AI are the five main threats to global financial stability. He said any slowdown in AI investment or earnings could cause a sharp repricing across the AI value chain, and that with highly autonomous AI tools "the most immediate concern is regarding cyber risks" for interconnected financial systems.
